## Summary

Nexar was incorporated in Israel on 5 January 2015 by Eran Shir and Bruno Fernandez-Ruiz, with its registered address at HaRakevet 58, Tel Aviv, and a US base in New York [2]. TechCrunch described it as Tel Aviv-based in January 2018, when it raised a 30 million US dollar Series B to build a vehicle-to-vehicle road-safety network; its app, launched in 2016, lets drivers use a phone as a dashcam [3]. The IEEE registry lists one MA-L block, C4:F1:22, to Nexar Ltd. at the HaRakevet Street address [1].

A MAC in this block is most likely a Nexar dash cam such as the Nexar Beam, a screenless 1080p camera whose settings can be changed only from the Nexar Android or iOS app [4][5]. Nexar's own specification for the Beam lists an Allwinner V3 processor, 256 MB DDR3, a GalaxyCore GC2053 sensor, a Bosch BMI160 G-sensor and 802.11b/g/n/ac Wi-Fi on 2.4 and 5 GHz, so expect the camera to appear as a Wi-Fi device or hotspot paired with a driver's phone inside a vehicle [4][5].

Malwarebytes reported on 5 September 2025 that a hacker had reached Nexar's AWS store of more than 130 TB of dashcam video because an access key embedded in every dashcam carried excessive privileges; Nexar fixed it after 404 Media contacted the company [6]. The FCC ID databases refused this session's requests, so no grantee code is listed, and no source documents MAC randomization.
